claim: *Multiple routes to engineering models.* A model may be constructed from requirements and intent, recovered from existing systems and experience, or discovered through agent exploration—the routes are alternatives, not stages. However it arrives, the model carries engineering knowledge and the selected obligations drawn from it, and it serves three uses: engineers reason and design through it, agents are directed by it, and results are evaluated and checked against it. A model recovered from an implementation describes what exists; it does not establish that the observed design is desirable, and the engineer decides which discovered properties become obligations. Modeling is not a prescribed phase before implementation: engineering continues, and further discoveries may motivate new or revised models.

alt: Three routes arrive at modeling from above and three uses leave it below. The incoming routes are requirements and intent, agent exploration and discovery, and existing systems and experience. Each joins one full-width rail, so none is privileged and none is a stage before another; a single arrow carries the rail into modeling. Modeling yields engineering models, which hold knowledge and the selected obligations drawn from it. From the model, one rail fans out to three uses: reason and design, direct agent work, and evaluate and check. Those three rejoin a rail that continues downward to further engineering, because engineering does not stop at the model: later discoveries may motivate new or revised models. The horizontal rails are collection bars, not process edges.
